chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the woman who copulates with her husband and then she menstruates while she is in the bathroom — should she perform ghusl or not? He said: 'That which invalidates salat has come to her, so she does not need to perform ghusl.'

key_terms.الْمُغْتَسَلِ: The bathing place or bathroom — the location where ritual washing is performed
key_terms.تَغْتَسِلُ: To perform ghusl — the full ritual bath required after major ritual impurity
key_terms.يُجَامِعُهَا زَوْجُهَا: Her husband copulates with her — establishing the context of janabah (major ritual impurity)
key_terms.يُفْسِدُ الصَّلَاةَ: That which invalidates/spoils salat — here referring to haydh (menstruation), which prevents a woman from performing prayer

ai.seo_question: If a woman begins menstruating while in the bathroom after intercourse with her husband, does she need to perform ghusl?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) was asked a jurisprudential question: if a woman begins menstruating while already in the bathroom preparing for or performing ghusl after intercourse, must she complete the ghusl? The Imam ruled that she is exempt, because menstruation itself is the greater state of ritual impurity that nullifies salat, and the ghusl of janabah (major ritual impurity from intercourse) is superseded by haydh. This ruling reflects the principle that once haydh begins, the obligation of ghusl al-janabah is suspended until after the menstrual period ends.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Yahya Al Kahily, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws about the woman who copulates with her husband, and (then) she menstruates while she is in the bathroom. Should she wash or not wash?’ Heasws said: ‘There has come to her what spoils her Salaat, so she does not (need to) wash (for the Salaat)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd Allah ibn Yahya al-Kahiliy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a woman who after sexual relation with her husband experiences Hayd (menses) and she is already in the bath area. Must she take Ghusl (bath) or not? He (the Imam) said, ‘Something which invalidates Salah (prayer) has come with her. She does not need Ghusl (bath).’”
